elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: If oxygen saturation < 94% or respiratory rate ≥ 30, give face mask oxygen.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: Keep patient nil by mouth until swallowing is formally assessed.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: Check glucose: if < 3 (< 4 if diabetes) 19.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: Avoid treating BP ≥ 140/90 as this may worsen stroke. If BP ≥ 220/120, discuss with specialist about need for pre-referral treatment.

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: Decide where to refer the patient depending on when symptoms started:

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: If patient can reach hospital within 3 hours of onset of symptoms, refer urgently for thrombolysis to specialist stroke unit (if available).

elements.section: Give urgent attention to the patient with a new stroke/TIA:
elements.text: If patient cannot reach hospital within 3 hours of symptoms onset, refer same day and give single dose aspirin 300mg if fully conscious and can swallow (avoid if on long-term anticoagulant or headache/neck stiffness).

Sudden onset of one or more of the following suggests a stroke (or a transient ischaemic attack (TIA) if symptoms lasted < 24 hours and resolved completely): • Weakness or numbness of face/arm/leg, especially on one side of the body • Blurred or decreased vision in one/both eyes or double vision • Difficulty speaking or understanding • Difficulty walking, dizziness, loss of balance or co-ordination

Advise the patient with stroke/TIA • Educate the patient that stroke/TIA is a brain attack. Quick treatment of a minor stroke or TIA can reduce the risk of a major stroke. Refer to available helpline/s 200. • If < 55 years (man) or < 65 years (woman), advise the first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) to have CVD risk assessment 142. • Avoid oral contraceptives containing oestrogen. Advise other method such as copper IUD, injectable, progestogen-only pill 170.

Treat the patient with stroke/TIA • Give influenza vaccine 0.5mL IM yearly. • Give aspirin 150mg daily for life. Avoid if < 30 years, haemorrhagic stroke, previous peptic ulcer, dyspepsia or on anticoagulant. If prosthetic heart valve, valvular heart disease or atrial fibrillation, refer for warfarin instead. • If patient had an ischaemic stroke, give rosuvastatin 10mg daily for life, regardless of cholesterol. If patient develops muscle pain/cramps, reduce dose to 5mg daily. If no improvement and not on LPVr/ATVr/DRVr switch to simvastatin 10mg at night or discuss with specialist. Avoid if pregnant or breastfeeding.
Assess the patient with previous stroke/TIA

Symptoms Every visit Ask about chest pain 24 or leg pain 80.
Mental health Every visit If stress, anxiety or low mood 98.
Rehabilitation needs Every visit Refer to physiotherapist for mobility/self care; occupational therapist for self care; speech therapist for swallowing/coughing after eating/ speaking/drooling.
Palliative care Every visit Assess need for palliative care 191.
BP Every visit If known hypertension 149. If not, and BP ≥ 140/90 148.
Fingerprick glucose At diagnosis and yearly If known diabetes 145. If not known with diabetes 19.
Fasting cholesterol and triglycerides At diagnosis if not already done If cholesterol > 7.5 or triglycerides > 10, check TSH and refer to doctor.
HIV At diagnosis, especially if < 50 years Test for HIV 124. If known HIV, give routine care 126.
ECG At diagnosis if not already done If abnormal, discuss/refer.
